sources.title: Data Centres as Enabling Infrastructure
sources.notes: November 2025; commissioned for Data Centres Australia by AirTrunk, Amazon Web Services, CDC and NEXTDC, and prepared by Mandala. Archived 2026-10-14 at data/raw/operators/mandala/ with a SHA-256 manifest; the PDF and its text are not committed (a commercial report). CertifiedStrategic.com names it as the source of the 1,350 MW (2024) and 3,100 MW (2030) deployable capacity figures; its text states neither, and it cites Mandala's October 2024 report, Empowering Australia's Digital Future, for the earlier analysis. Cited by RG-100 for that finding, not for any figure.

set.summary: Certified Strategic is the framework's highest level: the register calls it 'the highest level of assurance to Australian Government customers'. CertifiedStrategic.com adds that it is required for sensitive and PROTECTED workloads, which no primary source here states. The register lists 21 Certified Strategic facilities and 41 enclaves across 14 providers (archive of 2026-09-28), and states that registration of prospective providers and supplementary assessments are paused from 3 November 2025 until the framework's reforms are complete. Which agency administers the framework is not established from a primary source here: the register names only 'the Department', and releases up to v2.2.0 named the Digital Transformation Agency on an aggregator's authority, which is withdrawn (RG-100).

add_sources.quote: Strategic Certification enclave and facility providers represents the highest level of assurance to Australian Government customers and offers the most secure storage solutions for government held data. | The Department will pause the HCF Certification registration of prospective service providers and HCF Certified providers seeking supplementary assessment effective from 3 November 2025 until HCF reforms have been completed. HCF Certified providers will not be impacted.

set.notes: Named by CertifiedStrategic.com (March 2026) as administrator of the Hosting Certification Framework (Certified Strategic / Certified Assured). That attribution is withdrawn: it rests on a grade C aggregator, and the register itself names only 'the Department'. Which agency administers the framework today is open (RG-100).

Six HCF Certified Strategic sites: enclaves IC1, IC2, IC3 and IC3e in Sydney and facilities IC4 and IC5 at Fairbairn (ACT), plus a certified Government Cloud Service; the only provider the register lists for both data centres and a cloud service. CORRECTED 2026-10-14: releases up to v2.2.0 said five sites, omitting IC3e.

The 162 MW IT capacity, A$2bn cost and approval date came from a grade C aggregator article. NEXTDC's own M4 page gives 150 MW of IT capacity and calls the facility 'Currently In Planning' (operator_sources pack); which capacity stands is for a human to settle (RG-100).

research_gaps.question: Replace CertifiedStrategic.com (SRC_CERTSTRAT) for what still rests on it alone: four national capacity figures it relays second-hand (deployable 1,350 MW in 2024 and 3,100 MW by 2030, attributed to Mandala; live 1,400 MW in 2025 and 1,800 MW by 2028, attributed to CBRE), the locations and descriptions in five provider notes that the register does not state, the framework's PROTECTED requirement, M4's approval date and cost, and a primary source or removal for ENT_VANTAGE and ENT_AUSTRALIANSUPER; and settle NEXTDC M4's IT capacity, 162 MW from the article against 150 MW on NEXTDC's own page.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: When reviewed, the article was the sole source for 27 of the 93 sites and 25 of the 26 Certified Strategic flags. Batches S3 and S4 confirmed every flag against the Commonwealth register (RG-096) and cited operators' own pages, so no site rests on it alone. What remains is aggregate and descriptive, and two of its citations proved not to be in it at all.
research_gaps.target_source: Mandala Partners, Empowering Australia's Digital Future (October 2024); CBRE, AI Adoption Drives Australia's Data Centre Investment and Demand (August 2025); NEXTDC's ASX announcement and the Victorian Government's record of the M4 approval; the DigitalBridge/Vantage release on AustralianSuper's 2023 investment
research_gaps.notes: ADVANCED 2026-10-14. Archived and read the article itself (version of 2026-10-02): it does not mention Vantage, AustralianSuper, AirTrunk SYD3 or Stockland, so the two entities' claims are withdrawn and the two sites now take their better sources as primary. Re-sourced to the register: the provider counts in the Equinix, Digital Realty, Macquarie (now six sites, adding IC3e), DCI and Telstra notes, the framework's 'highest level of assurance' wording, and the Macquarie security record, which is derived from the register and now VERIFIED. Marsden Park's application row now cites the portal and its assessment report. The Mandala report the article names (Data Centres as Enabling Infrastructure, November 2025, archived) does not state 1,350 MW or 3,100 MW; it points to Mandala's October 2024 report, which this environment cannot fetch because the host's robots.txt refuses it, as does CDC's copy. CBRE answers 403. FROM THE ARCHIVED REGISTER (primary, SRC_HCF_REGISTER): it lists data centre facilities that match no site record here: Australian Data Centres ADC Mitchell (facility); Australian Data Centres ADC Fyshwick (enclave); Cloud Carrier DB1 (facility); DigiCo BNE2 (facility); DigiCo ADL1, SYD1 (enclave); Macquarie Technology Group IC3e (enclave); Fujitsu Australia Western Sydney, Homebush (enclave); NEXTDC Brisbane 1, Brisbane 2 (enclave); Springfield Real Estate Sales Pty Ltd Polaris Data Centre (enclave); Vocus TransACT House Dickson (enclave). RG-096 matched only existing records, so these are candidates for new site rows. LEADS ONLY, from search-engine summaries read on 2026-10-14 (below grade D, not relied on, and kept out of every fact row): the framework appears to have moved from the Digital Transformation Agency to the Department of Home Affairs on 1 May 2023; the 1,350 MW and 3,100 MW figures appear to come from Mandala's October 2024 report; and AustralianSuper appears to have announced a EUR 1.5bn minority investment in Vantage Data Centers' EMEA platform on 11 September 2023.
